definitions.explanation: Suffix attaching to a noun to form the name of a historical field or written history. Common in academic, journalistic, and book-title vocabulary.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}{史|し}を{勉強|べんきょう}している。
{世界|せかい}{史|し}の{授業|じゅぎょう}が{好|す}きだ。
{現代|げんだい}{美術|びじゅつ}{史|し}の{概論|がいろん}を{大学|だいがく}で{受講|じゅこう}した。
examples.english: I took an introductory course on modern art history at university.

notes:
Names the history of a country, field, era, or institution. Productive in academic and book titles.

COMPOUNDS:
- {日本|にほん}{史|し}: Japanese history
- {世界|せかい}{史|し}: world history
- {美術|びじゅつ}{史|し}: art history
- {現代|げんだい}{史|し}: modern history
- {古代|こだい}{史|し}: ancient history
- {会社|かいしゃ}{史|し}: company history

USAGE:
Also used in academic field names: {歴史|れきし}{学|がく} (the discipline of history) vs. ~{史|し} (a specific historical subject). In Japanese high school, students typically choose between {日本|にほん}{史|し} and {世界|せかい}{史|し}.
